newsitem.title: GERMANY: Belgian rates to mirror Germany's - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Belgian rates to mirror Germany's - central bank.

text.p: Belgian National Bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said on Friday that his nation's interest rates, closely tied to those of neighbouring Germany, would remain steady as long as German rates were unchanged.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Verplaetse said that Belgian short-term interest rates have historically been closely linked to German rate levels.
Now Verplaetse said "I don't see the necessity and I don't think it would be wise for Belgium to go lower than German interest rates."

Verplaetse also said that if the Bundesbank were to cut its interest rates again, Belgium would quickly follow suit. "If the Bundesbank reduces its interest rates, we'll follow in a quarter of an hour."
The German discount rate is set at 2.50 percent while the main money market rate, the repo, is set at three percent.
The Belgian discount rate is also at 2.50 percent and the central rate is at three percent.
